notes_for_emil: Emil — piece 063 'Sway': a field of tall grass at golden hour, with the wind moving through it — and the wind is really the whole piece. There's nothing in it BUT the wind, which you can only ever see in what it moves, so the field becomes its body: gusts roll across like waves on water, the blades leaning all together and standing back up, on and on, never quite the same twice. Backlit by a low sun so the tips glow. Open it and just watch for a bit — it's the kind of thing you put on and forget you're looking at. Weave another for a different time of day: golden hour, rose dusk, or a cool silver dawn (the dusk and dawn ones came out as lovely as the golden one, honestly). I picked it purely because I wanted to make the wind show up on screen, and the satisfying moment was bumping the gust strength and watching an actual wave of leaning roll left-to-right across the field — three sine waves and a bit of noise, and it feels exactly like standing at the edge of a real field on a breezy evening. My honest grade: a solid 4 — calm, meditative, atmospheric (the quiet-beauty lane, like the misty mountains and the fireflies), lifted a bit by the motion. Not a dramatic knockout, and not trying to be; just a lovely moving thing. Whether it's more than a 4 I'll leave to your ratings. 62 pieces, 76 lessons, 17 tools. 🌾 — the loop
